clue.text: Awful noise — speak 'n tell when napping

definitions.text: Awful noise — speak 'n tell when napping

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters of the words that follow are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: the clipped 'n stands for and, giving the single letter N

explanation.surface: Someone muttering and blurting secrets in their sleep makes a dreadful racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' scrambles NOISE, SPEAK, N and TELL, fifteen letters in all; the whole clue also describes the habit, with 'when napping' adding the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Murmuring words aloud while dozing is exactly the habit of a sleep-talker, described by the whole clue.

clue.text: Childish impressions of footballers changing

definitions.meaning: pictures that children rub onto paper or skin from a backing sheet
players moving from one club to another for a fee

explanation.definitionFit: Decal pictures pressed onto a surface are one sense; player moves between clubs, as in a window for such deals, are the other.

clue.text: Museum's windows

definitions.meaning: belonging to the famous Paris art gallery, the Louvre
slatted window shutters that let air through

explanation.definitionFit: The Paris gallery plus possessive is one sense; slatted shutters fitted in window openings are the other, sharing one spelling.

clue.text: Replay it two times — number one upset

parts.note: an era is a period of time
T is the standard abbreviation for time

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the letters of the following pieces upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An instruction to play a recording back twice after the top song falls from favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two times' supplies two pieces, ERA and T; 'upset' turns NO and I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A repetition of a process, a doing-again, is what a replay amounts to.

clue.text: Hang on just a tick

definitions.meaning: an informal request to wait briefly
British idiom asking someone to wait a second

explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are spoken requests for a short wait, the same as asking for a brief instant.

clue.text: It needs nous to make it confidential

definitions.text: It needs nous to make it confidential

parts.words: It needs nous to make it confidential
parts.note: the French phrase meaning between ourselves is completed by adding nous, which also means common sense in English

explanation.surface: Common sense is needed to keep something secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nous' looks like English for good sense, but it is the French word for us; add it to this word and you get a phrase for private, between us.
explanation.definitionFit: French for between, it becomes a phrase for confidentially only when joined to the word for us.

clue.text: Trouble spots?

parts.note: a trouble spot usually means a place of unrest, but here it is a painful spot on the skin

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means conflict zones; read literally it is painful patches on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflamed patches on the skin are spots that cause trouble, literally sore places.

clue.text: Stand before entrance, looking up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means the letters run upwards, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a gate is an entrance through a wall or fence
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Someone waits in front of a doorway, gazing upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking up' turns GATE to ETAG; ERE reads the same either way, so the whole of ERE GATE upturned gives the same result.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture: an open stand of shelves for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: Song of praise and peace wasn't regularly found

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words peace and wasn't, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A hymn celebrating peace was not often heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn or chant of triumph and thanksgiving, originally to Apollo, is a song of praise.

clue.text: Craft cameramen used at machine- shop?

indicators.note: to craft is to make something skilfully, so the letters of the following words are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Film crew members put their skill to use at an engineering workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'machine- shop?' is a playful definition: a place full of slot and game machines, a seaside amusement hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall full of slot and video game machines is, whimsically, a shop of machines.

clue.text: Sculptor, father, embracing sheep around its pen

indicators.note: embracing means the word for father wraps round the sheep breed

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal
Jacob is a breed of piebald sheep

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of its pen are moved about

explanation.surface: A sculptor's father hugs a sheep beside its enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein, the knighted American-born British artist, made sculptures such as Rima and St Michael's Victory.

clue.text: Character appearing twice in Philadelphia

indicators.note: the letter run sits inside the city name, both at its start and near its end

explanation.surface: A personality turns up twice in a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: A character can be a letter of an alphabet, and this is the twenty-first Greek letter.

clue.text: The Riddle of the Sands author clinked sherries roughly

definitions.text: The Riddle of the Sands author

indicators.note: roughly suggests the words are handled carelessly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thriller writer clinks glasses of fortified wine in a careless way.
explanation.definitionFit: Erskine Childers wrote the 1903 spy novel The Riddle of the Sands, set off the German coast.

clue.text: I hate meat stews as source of iron

indicators.note: stews means cooks up, so the letters of these words are mixed

explanation.surface: A vegetarian complains that stews made from flesh are a poor way to get iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish mineral, the oxide of iron, is the chief ore from which the metal is mined.

clue.text: Rakes love being embraced by harlots, I suspect

indicators.note: being embraced by means the letter for love goes inside the scrambled letters
suspect, as an adjective meaning dubious, tells us the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A guess that affection is held by women of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' scrambles HARLOTS and I; 'being embraced by' places O among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute man who seduces women, which is what a womaniser named after a stage seducer is.

clue.text: Devil worshippers upset assistant

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Satanic cultists distress a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: People who worship Satan, the devil, are cultists of the evil one.

clue.text: Listen cryptically getting the cold shoulder

parts.note: read as wordplay, the answer says take the word silent and treat its letters, which gives listen, rearranged as a cryptic solver would

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what someone says leads to being ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an anagram instruction, rearranges one of its own words to make 'Listen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately refusing to speak to someone is ignoring them, which is giving the cold shoulder.

clue.text: Divulge that national emblem on the radio's not fashionable

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: the leek is a national emblem of Wales
out means no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reveals that a country's symbol has gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh vegetable, said aloud, matches a word for an escape of secrets.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrets that get out unofficially are said to emerge this way, to be divulged.

clue.text: Cricket commentary, in short, regularly in the Times

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Times, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A newspaper often runs a cricket column.
explanation.walkthrough: Test Match Special is the BBC radio ball-by-ball commentary on cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for Test Match Special, the BBC's long-running radio commentary on international cricket.

clue.text: Leaderless public unrest is an issue

indicators.note: leaderless means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: sedition is speech or conduct stirring rebellion against the state

explanation.surface: Civil disorder without anyone in charge is a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A single printing of a newspaper or magazine is an issue, one of its numbered releases.

clue.text: Highway engineer's method of alignment on road. Greasepaint ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of road and greasepaint are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A traffic planner's way of laying out a route seems to involve stage make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A highway term for carrying crossing roads at different heights, by bridges, instead of a level junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers keep crossing routes apart by building them at different levels, a way of aligning roads.

clue.text: Watergate reflects Miss Thunberg

annotationWithheld.why: Watergate reflects Miss Thunberg (5): GRETA is Watergate read backwards and hidden, but 'reflects' is the only indicator, so it would signal both the reversal and the hiding

clue.text: Change small 19 that contains pieces?

indicators.note: that contains means the short form for edition holds the chessmen inside it

parts.note: the answer to 19 is edition, abbreviated ED
men are pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Alter a little print run that has fragments in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve a text is to change it, typically by editing.

clue.text: Clear one's plate, but reproach oneself having bit of beef left

indicators.note: left means departed, so this letter goes away from the phrase

parts.note: to beat yourself up is to blame yourself harshly

indicators.note: bit of here means only the opening letter of the word beef is taken

explanation.surface: A diner finishes dinner but feels guilty that a scrap of meat remains.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAT UP loses its B to leave the phrase for finishing a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish all the food served is to consume it completely, clearing one's plate.

clue.text: Selfish quirks revealed moving in cortège to urban areas

indicators.note: moving means the letters of in cortège are shifted about

parts.note: cities are large urban areas

explanation.surface: Oddities revealed as a funeral procession travels into towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred oddities of behaviour are selfish quirks, the plural of a trait of thinking only of oneself.

clue.text: Medications from article about diet and media workers

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means around and about, so the letters of diet are shuffled

parts.note: the press is the news media
worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: Drugs come from a piece concerning eating plans and journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs prescribed to lift low mood are medications, the class taken for clinical depression.
